# Best Dividend-paying Assets Are Covered-Call ETFs, Expert Says


By:[Paul Dykewicz](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/author/pdykewicz-admin/)


, November 13, 2026


Link copied!


The best[dividend-paying](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/three-dividend-paying-investments-featured-at-baron-conference/) assets are covered-call ETFs due to market volatility that is expanding option premiums, said Bryan Perry, who heads the high-income-producing[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) investment newsletter that averages a dividend yield of more than 10%.


Perry described the investing as a covered-call overlay strategy, in which fund managers actively sell short-dated, out-of-the-money listed call options against the holdings on an exchange-traded fund (ETF). By writing options across staggered strike prices, the fund harvests option premiums to distribute regular monthly cash flow to shareholders but still preserves partial upside participation the related stocks rally, Perry added.


“Because call writing trades away extreme upside potential in exchange for upfront premium income, the strategy is engineered to thrive in range-bound, choppy or mildly bullish equity environments,” Perry wrote in his[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) investment newsletter. Perry also heads the[Breakout Blue Chip Trader](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/breakout-blue-chip-trader-web-default/?source=GURUBBCT1) ,[Quick Income Trader](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/qit-default/?source=GURUQIT1) and[Hi-Tech Trader](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/htt-default/?source=GURUHTT1) advisory services that recommend both stocks and options.


*Bryan Perry heads[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) .*


**Best Dividend-paying Assets Are Covered-Call ETFs: JEPI**


One of the best in class funds is JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF (NYSEARCA: JEPI), which seeks to deliver monthly distributable income and Nasdaq 100 exposure with reduced volatility, Perry opined. The fund’s portfolio managers, Hamilton Reiner and Eric Moreau, use a data science approach to fundamental research and portfolio construction with a goal of delivering a lower beta, lower volatility experience versus the Nasdaq 100 Index.


Rather than forcing income investors to rely on broad-market covered-call funds, JEPI offers income a potent distribution yield of 11.96%. Some covered-call ETFs are generating strong total returns, without suffering the destructive net asset value (NAV) erosion that plagues many high-yield derivative funds, he added.


The fund constructs a long equity portfolio through a proprietary data science-driven investment approach designed to maximize risk-adjusted returns. The ETF also seeks to deliver less volatility than the Nasdaq-100 Index, aside from providing monthly income.


The fund combines large-cap technology stocks and a covered-call strategy with its investing strategy. It also has $42.5 billion in assets.

**Best Dividend-paying Assets Are Covered-Call ETFs: SPYI**


The NEOS S&P 500 High Income ETF (CBOE: SPYI) holds S&P 500 stocks and sells index call options to generate monthly distributions. Also favored by Perry, the fund had $12.5 billion in assets and a 1.43% distribution yield as of November 13, 2026.


The fund offers a current distribution yield of 11.43% and seeks to distribute high monthly income produced by investing in the parts of the S&P 500 Index, while using a data-driven call option strategy. Actively managed by NEOS, SPYI aims to pursue tax loss harvesting opportunities in addition to utilizing SPX Index options classified as section 1256 contracts, which are subject to reduced tax rates.


SPYI’s call option strategy can include both sold and purchased SPX index options, which may provide the opportunity for upside capture in rising equity markets. The NEOS S&P 500 High Income ETF seeks high monthly income in a tax efficient manner, with the potential for upside appreciation in rising markets.

**Woods’ Wisdom about Investing After Midterm Elections**


Reasons for optimism in the market include the continued growth of artificial intelligence, said Jim Woods, who heads the *[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS)* investment newsletter, as well as the[TNT Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tnt-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUTNT) ,[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=GURUTT01) ,[Five Star Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/five-star-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUFST) and[Bullseye Stock Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/bullseye-default/?source=GURUBEST1) advisory services that recommend stocks and options. He cited a Bespoke Investment Group study of historical returns of the S&P 500 after a bull market’s four-year anniversary found that the median return in the following 12 months reached 16.8%.


As far as money and investments, markets tend to be indifferent to midterm election results, Woods wrote in the November 2026 issue of *[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS)* . From a historical perspective, the volatility usually occurs prior to the midterm elections, he added.


*Jim Woods heads[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS) and[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=GURUTT01) .*


“We’ve already seen that volatility so far this year, and, of course, the volatility has been exaggerated by the U.S.-Iran war, a volatile AI build-out frenzy and a Fed that’s in rate hike mode,” Woods wrote. “Yet historically speaking, midterm election years do tend to be more volatile than other years.”


For instance, the average S&P 500 drawdown in midterm election years is 19%, whereas, in the other three years of the presidential cycle, it averages 12%, Woods continued. This year has been light on drawdowns, even with some volatility, with the S&P 500’s max drawdown of 9.1% since the first quarter of 2026, he added.


After midterm elections, the market tends to perform extremely well, Woods commented. Proof comes from the historical record, according to Sevens Report Research, he added.


“First, since 1950, November is the S&P 500’s second-best performing month in midterm years, with the domestic equity benchmark up an average of 2.7% on the month while trending higher 79% of the time,” Woods reported. “Second, going back to 1974, the S&P 500 averaged a 5.7% return in the three months following midterms, and the index was positive 85% of the time,” he continued.


“Impressively, in the six months following midterm elections, the S&P 500 had an average return of 12.4%, and it was up an incredible 100% of the time,” Woods wrote. “Want more supporting evidence? Well, consider that from 1930-2026, the S&P 500 *never* declined in the 12 months following a midterm election, with an average return of 14% (considerably higher than the S&P 500’s historical average annual return of 10.5%).”

**Geopolitical Risk**


Russian forces have stepped up their attacks against Ukrainian civilians. A Russian drone struck the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro as people waited to board a train on Oct. 29, killing 15 people. An additional 10 people were wounded in the strike, the latest in a series of Russian attacks on transport and energy infrastructure in Ukraine that have targeted civilians. At least 19 people, including two 15-year-old girls, were killed across the country on that day, Ukrainian authorities said.


Russia’s persistent invasion of Ukraine has included firing on buses and other civilian targets with jet-powered attack drones. Ukraine’s capital of Kyiv has been targeted directly, causing the death of women, children and other civilians. In response, more than a dozen automated turrets have been deployed around the Ukrainian capital as Russia steps up its use of faster drones that are more difficult for conventional air defenses to intercept.


Ukraine’s Air Force indicated it is using artificial intelligence and machine vision to track targets and aim through its[Sky Sentinel system](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U5muTgzi-04) to defend against the faster Russian jet-powered drones, creating a tactical battle in which warfare is moving towards machines fighting machines. The war’s escalation occurred despite recent visits to both nation’s capitals by President Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who sought to broker a peace agreement.


**Options Advisory Service Offers Alternative to Stocks**


Investors who are wary about the ups and downs of the stock market can explore option trading as an alternative. An options advisory service that offers a pure-play alternative for those who want to trade into volatility to pursue quick profits is the[DayTradeSPY](https://daytradespy.com/offer/trading-room-default-editorial/?source=GURUTR1) Trading Room, advised Hugh Grossman, the service’s senior leader. The[DayTradeSPY Trading Room](https://daytradespy.com/offer/trading-room-default-editorial/?source=GURUTR1) has a win rate that averages 89.8%, its[Pick of the Day](https://daytradespy.com/offer/pick-of-the-day-default/?source=GURUPOD1) service track record is 88.6% and the[DayTradeSPY Signal](https://daytradespy.com/offer/daytradespy-signal-default/?source=DTSSIGGURU) service profits 86% of the time.


As long as there is turmoil in the world… wars, tariffs, political upheaval, you name it, “we make money,” said Grossman, who also offers[Inner Circle](https://daytradespy.com/offer/inner-circle-default/?source=GURUIC1) memberships that include all his services.


“We can’t control the events of the day, but we can take advantage of that instability by trading short-term movements,” Grossman continued. “Options on SPY provide outstanding leverage and liquidity for quick profits.”
